hints: Look at the size of each organelle in the table and remember what a light microscope at x400 can actually resolve, think big and coloured versus tiny.
Recall the resolution limit of a light microscope is about 200 nm, so which of these four is several micrometres long and green?
walkthrough:
**Remember the limit of the light microscope**

Think of the light microscope as having blurry vision for very small things. Its resolution limit is about $200 \text{ nm}$.

Anything much smaller than this will not be clearly visible, even at high power ($\times 400$).

**Sort the organelles by size**

Ribosomes are tiny, about $20 \text{ nm}$ in diameter. Centrioles are about $200 \text{ nm}$ wide. The membranes of endoplasmic reticulum are also too thin to resolve clearly.

Chloroplasts are huge in comparison, about $5 \text{ } \mu\text{m}$ long, green, and easy to spot in plant cells.

**Match to the table**

So only chloroplasts get a tick for clearly visible. Ribosomes, endoplasmic reticulum and centrioles all get a cross.

That pattern is ribosomes X, ER X, centrioles X, chloroplasts tick, which is row D.

options.A: Incorrect, ribosomes and ER are far too small to be clearly resolved with light at x400, and chloroplasts would be visible but are marked X here.
options.B: Incorrect, ribosomes and centrioles are below or at the resolution limit so cannot be clearly seen, and visible chloroplasts are wrongly marked X.
options.C: Incorrect, ER and centrioles need an electron microscope for clear detail, only the chloroplast tick in this row is right.
options.D: Correct, only chloroplasts are large enough (micrometres, green) to be clearly visible at x400, the other three need electron microscopy.
